name: figma-photo-strap-backplate
story: A designer drew a name strap whose BACKPLATE is a photograph - the picture is the panel, not a portrait square beside it - set the name and role on top of it, put a thin amber tab down its left edge, and exported the frame as SVG.
idioms: the panel itself is the placed picture: <rect id="Strap backplate" fill="url(#pattern0_51_204)"/>, not a positioned <image>
<pattern patternContentUnits="objectBoundingBox" width="1" height="1"> holding <use xlink:href="#image0_51_204" transform="scale(0.5)">
the actual <image> with the base64 data: URI is parked LAST inside <defs>, carrying only width/height and xlink:href
the layer name stays on the visible rect; the <image> in defs is called image0_51_204
a 10px accent tab drawn at the panel's own left edge - the second rectangle in the file, and the only other one
frame with no fill exports with no backplate rect - the strap is transparent over video
no <?xml?> prolog, zero indentation, fill="none" on the root, uppercase hex, xml:space="preserve" plus style="white-space: pre" on text
whyThisMatters: docs/SVG_AUTHORING.md makes the designer two promises about this one rectangle - an embedded picture filling a shape you drew is a picture field, and a panel drawn as a rectangle is the one that can grow - and says nothing anywhere about having to choose between them. A photo-filled backplate is an ordinary thing to draw, so if being offered as a picture takes the shape out of the growth inventory, the long name has nowhere to go and the only rectangle left to offer is a 10px tab that can never grow. That is sweep finding 7.
